summary: Attacked the Analytic number theory area — AnalyticNumberTheory, ArithmeticStatistics, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries: 7 roadmaps, 51 stages and 69 accepted paper routes from 33 papers, the richest area I have red-teamed. Three findings, two medium and one low, and all three are omissions the atlas's own records already half-document: the arithmetic-scheme form of Chebotarev density has no owner although two papers need it and one of their routes is unaccepted for exactly that reason; Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters is named by nothing, as one route says in so many words; and Stevenhagen's conjecture is unnamed. Four other heads came back clean, and this area is unusually well built — the routing asserts ownership rather than assuming it, the conjecture registers are explicit, and every roadmap's prerequisites match its stage edges exactly.
checked: All 51 stages of the seven roadmaps, with their descriptions, inputs and acceptance clauses, and the accepted audit verdict for each: 7 built, 19 partly built, 24 not built, 1 process.
Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the papers this session has reviewed routes into this area, checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files.

All 69 routes and their reasons in full, from 33 papers, with the stage distribution: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 12, ST.5 11, AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 9, ST.3 7, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2 6, AN.5 6, AN.2 5, ST.2 5, and 22 of the 51 stages receiving none.

Dependency bookkeeping, the head that produced a finding in part 1 of the Algebraic number theory area. It is clean here and more strictly so: for every one of the six campaign roadmaps, `prerequisites` equals its set of cross-roadmap stage-edge heads exactly, with no extras and no omissions — AnalyticNumberTheory 7 of 7, ArithmeticStatistics 5 of 5, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod 3 of 3, ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory 3 of 3, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns 1 of 1, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence 1 of 1.

ArithmeticStatistics' empty `consumers`, which looked like that same finding because it is the most heavily routed roadmap in the area with 30 routes. It is correct: the only five roadmaps in either directory that cite ArithmeticStatistics are precisely its own five prerequisites, citing it as their consumer, so it is a sink. The same holds for ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory.

Duplication, where the sharpest candidate was a near-collision of names: ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory:PM.3 'Metric Diophantine approximation' against the whole DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence roadmap. The division is deliberate and stated in PM's own summary — 'Almost-everywhere assertions, averages over integers, and statements about every real number remain distinct. Specify the probability space and measure before every distribution theorem.' PM.3 owns limsup sets, Borel-Cantelli, Khintchine and Duffin-Schaeffer-type theorems with Lebesgue and Hausdorff measures and the convergence and divergence halves separated; DT owns heights and irrationality exponents, Liouville and Roth, the subspace theorem, and transcendence. Continued fractions appear in both for different purposes, PM.4 for the Gauss map and ergodic metric statistics and DT.0 to connect them to Dirichlet approximation. Nothing is planned twice.

Whether any stage plans to prove a conjecture, which for an analytic area is the obvious way to state an unmeetable target. None does, and the guards are explicit: AN.6 maintains 'a statement register for RH, GRH, prime tuples and general functorial analytic continuation' and requires that 'a conditional statement exposes its hypothesis in its type'; AN.9 says 'Distinguish spectral RH analogues from Riemann RH' and 'A partition-function identity with zeta is not a proof of a zero-location conjecture'; PM.5 keeps 'Chowla/Sarnak-type general statements in the conjecture register' and forbids using 'a heuristic random model ... as a proven joint distribution'; AN.8 restricts itself to 'exact proved cases'; ST.3 requires that 'a heuristic moment is not substituted for a proven limit'.

The library boundary. All 51 stages are already audited, so as in the Elementary area the audit carries the library mapping and a red team's job is to break it where it is wrong rather than repeat it. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries is exemplary: 11 layers with 5 verdicted built and 6 partly built and none not built, a monotone progression (layers 0 to 4 built, 5 to 10 partly) matching its `active` lifecycle, and a summary that names the APIs it consumes — it 'regroups them by norm into Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction and LSeries APIs'. Its Layer 1 is titled 'norm fibres and Mathlib LSeries'. No stage in the area instructs construction of something an audit records as built.

The canonical named results of the field, checked in both directions — against both roadmap directories and against the 33 routed papers, because an absence only matters if the area's own sources need it. Cohen-Lenstra is named as a selected source of both ST.3 and ST.5; Malle appears in 23 roadmap files and 27 papers with 75 mentions; MacWilliams in 1.

The two absences I deliberately did not file, which is the discipline this head needs. Davenport-Heilbronn and Katz-Sarnak appear in no roadmap in either directory — and they are the archetypal results for ST.3 'Fields and class groups', so they are tempting. But neither is mentioned by a single one of the 33 routed papers, so filing them would be second-guessing the roadmap's scope rather than reporting a need its own sources demonstrate. Not findings.

A name collision that would have produced a wrong conclusion in either direction, caught by reading rather than counting. Searching the roadmaps for Heath-Brown returns one file, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod — but that is the Heath-Brown *identity*, a decomposition of the von Mangoldt function used in the prime-weighted circle-method branch ('construct a separate prime-weighted branch using Vaughan or Heath-Brown identities'). It is a different result from Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters, which is the subject of the second finding. This is the third time in this session that two theorems sharing a name have had to be separated, after Smyth's Mahler bound versus the trace problem and Salem numbers versus Salem-Spencer sets.

The restructuring record for both findings, since I cite it rather than inferring scope. RS-07.result.json gives AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 the action 'narrow' with keeps 'Arithmetic-to-analytic comparison maps for Dedekind/Hecke functions, boundary nonvanishing and prime-ideal applications, plus the Artin Euler-factor/induction int[erfaces]' — a number-field scope that does not extend to schemes of finite type over Z. The same proposal states that 'large-sieve/bilinear inequalities belong to SV.2'.

Whether the arithmetic-scheme density theorem is owned under other words, before calling it absent. Searched both roadmap directories for 'Frobenius density', 'N_X', 'arithmetic scheme', 'Serre ... Lectures' and 'finite type over Z'. Every hit is something else: 'Frobenius density' in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations is the tool used for Galois representations over a number field ('Prove uniqueness from Frobenius density using Chebotarev and continuity'), the 'N_X' hit is the Maslov index n_x(D) in HeegaardFloer, and every 'finite type over' hit is over a field, a DVR or another base in adic, moduli or ring-stack settings. The Chebotarev roadmap itself (14 stages, in part 1 of the sibling area) contains none of these phrases.

Library trees, with their sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 (Arithmetic-to-analytic comparison and prime-ideal applications), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: The arithmetic-scheme form of Chebotarev density — Frobenius density for normal integral rings of finite type over Z, Serre's theorem in Lectures on N_X(p) section 9 — has no owner. Two accepted paper extractions need it and route it to AN.4, and the atlas's own records already say AN.4 does not supply it: one of the two routes is recorded as an UNACCEPTED candidate for precisely this reason, and the accepted restructuring proposal RS-07 narrows AN.4 to number-field comparison maps and prime-ideal applications without assigning scheme-level density anywhere. Nothing else in either roadmap directory owns it, including the 14-stage Chebotarev roadmap, whose subject this would naturally extend. So a documented need sits between two roadmaps with no owner, and one route cannot be accepted until it has one.
findings.evidence: The unaccepted route, PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4, states the gap itself: 'UNACCEPTED candidate: the arithmetic-scheme Chebotarev input is not supplied by AN.4's number-field analytic comparison/prime-ideal interfaces. RS-07 narrows AN.4 and does not assign general finite-type arithmetic-scheme Frobenius density to it. A separate source-qualified supplier/extensi[on]'. The second need, PAPER-ABDURRAHMAN-VENKATESH-25 to AN.4: 'AN.4 keeps Chebotarev and its applications (RS-07). The density theorem for normal integral rings of finite type over Z (Serre, Lectures on N_X(p), section 9), used throughout section 2 and in section 2.14, is its arithmetic-scheme form; PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 sends the same statement there.' So the same statement is routed twice, once as an accepted need and once as a route that cannot be accepted. RS-07.result.json confirms the scope: 'AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4': {'action': 'narrow', 'keeps': 'Arithmetic-to-analytic comparison maps for Dedekind/Hecke functions, boundary nonvanishing and prime-ideal applications, plus the Artin Euler-factor/induction int[erfaces]'}. Ownership searches, run under several descriptions before concluding absence: 'Frobenius density' matches only IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, where it is the number-field tool for Galois determinants and representations ('Prove uniqueness from Frobenius density using Chebotarev and continuity'); 'N_X' matches only the Maslov index n_x(D) in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer; every match for 'finite type over' is over a field, a DVR or another base in adic, moduli and ring-stack roadmaps; and tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_Chebotarev.json contains none of 'finite type over', 'arithmetic scheme' or 'N_X(p)'.
findings.fix: Assign the arithmetic-scheme density theorem an owner and say which. The natural home is the Chebotarev roadmap, as a layer for the scheme-theoretic form: for a normal integral ring of finite type over Z, or equivalently a normal integral arithmetic scheme, the density of closed points whose Frobenius conjugacy class meets a given subset of the Galois group of a finite etale cover, in Serre's formulation in Lectures on N_X(p) section 9, with the number-field case recovered as the relative-dimension-zero instance. The alternative, if the analytic side is preferred, is a Part II extension of AN.4 explicitly scoped to arithmetic schemes, which is what PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16's route asks for; in that case RS-07's narrowing of AN.4 should be amended to say where the scheme-level statement lives, so the two routes stop pointing at a stage that disclaims them. Either way PAPER-ABDURRAHMAN-VENKATESH-25 and PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 are the sources, and the latter's route can then be accepted.

findings.claim: Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters is named by nothing in the atlas, although two accepted extractions route it to SV.2 and one of their route reasons says outright that SV.2 'does not yet name' it. SV.2 owns large-sieve inequalities generically — additive and multiplicative inequalities, duality, primitive-character reduction and Vaughan-style bilinear decompositions — but the papers need the sharper quadratic-character bound specifically, and the second route states that a generic result does not give it. So this is not a naming nicety: the target as written does not imply the theorem the sources require.
findings.evidence: PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO to SV.2: 'SV.2 plans the multiplicative large sieve and bilinear sums. The bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate the paper uses (Smith, Prop. 6.6) comes from Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters, a sharper member of that family that SV.2 does not yet name.' PAPER-SKOROBOGATOV-SOFOS-23 to SV.2: 'Heath-Brown's quadratic-character bilinear estimate belongs to the existing large-sieve/bilinear-sum layer. The prime-denominator 2 error and exact norms must be retained; a generic DFT or character-orthogonality theorem does not establish this bound.' SV.2's own description is: 'Prove additive and multiplicative large-sieve inequalities, duality, primitive-character reduction, and bilinear decompositions such as Vaughan identities', with source route 'KED-ANT Chapters 15-16 and Chapter 18 for Vaughan identity' — no quadratic-character large sieve and no Heath-Brown. Searching both roadmap directories for Heath-Brown returns exactly one file, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod, and that is a different theorem: the Heath-Brown *identity*, a von Mangoldt decomposition, in 'construct a separate prime-weighted branch using Vaughan or Heath-Brown identities, Type I/II estimates and uniform arithmetic-progression major-arc estimates'. RS-07.result.json confirms SV.2 is the right home for this family, stating that 'large-sieve/bilinear inequalities belong to SV.2'.
findings.fix: Name Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters as a target of SV.2, with the quadratic-character family, the sharper bound and the retained prime-denominator error and exact norms that PAPER-SKOROBOGATOV-SOFOS-23 requires, and record the bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate that PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO consumes (Smith, Proposition 6.6) as its consumer. SV.2's acceptance clause already says 'Orthogonality uses the correct character family', which is exactly the hypothesis this bound turns on, so the addition fits the stage as written; the two papers are its sources. The target should state explicitly that the generic multiplicative large sieve does not imply it, to stop a future worker discharging it by character orthogonality.

findings.claim: Stevenhagen's conjecture is named by no roadmap in either directory, although PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO mentions it 25 times and its route places the proven bounds towards it in ST.3. Severity is low: ST.3's target is 'selected counting and class-group moment/distribution theorems by discriminant and signature', and a density theorem for the solvability of the negative Pell equation is one of those, so the defect is that no target names the governing conjecture rather than that the material is unplanned. What makes it worth recording is that this area does name its governing conjectures elsewhere — Cohen-Lenstra is a declared source of ST.3 and ST.5, and Malle appears in 23 roadmap files — so by the area's own practice this one should be named too.
findings.evidence: PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO's route to ST.0, ST.3 and ST.5: 'ST.0 plans arithmetic families with local conditions, and D is one. ST.3 plans class-group distribution theorems, and the prior bounds towards Stevenhagen's conjecture (Fouvry-Kluners, CKMP, the authors' KP3) and the sets D_{2,n} belong there. ST.5 plans random-matrix distributions: MacWilliams' count of symmetric matrices over [F_2]'. The paper mentions Stevenhagen 25 times and PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21 twice, 27 in total across the 33 routed papers. A case-insensitive search of research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/ for Stevenhagen returns 0 files. For contrast, within the same two stages: ST.3's and ST.5's source route is 'Selected sources: BHARGAVA-SHANKAR, COHEN-LENSTRA', and Malle is named in 23 roadmap files. The same paper also routes the negative Pell equation itself to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4, so the set D-minus and its density are split across two areas by design; that split is fine, but it means neither side names the conjecture that governs the density.
findings.fix: Name Stevenhagen's conjecture in ST.3's target alongside Cohen-Lenstra: the conjectural density of discriminants for which the negative Pell equation is solvable, with the proven bounds towards it (Fouvry-Kluners, CKMP, and Koymans-Pagano's own) as the provable content and the conjecture itself kept in the register that ST.3's acceptance clause already implies by forbidding a heuristic moment to stand for a proven limit. The sets D_{2,n} should be recorded with it, and the cross-reference to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4, which owns the negative Pell equation, added so the two halves are connected.
